proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_step_two_of_black (m q N j : ℕ) (hNj : N ≤ j)
    (h0 : PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal m) q N)
    (h1 : PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal (m + 1)) q N)
    (hblack : leftDiagonal (m + 1) (j + 1) = true)
    (hblack2 : leftDiagonal (m + 2) (j + 1) = true) :
    PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal (m + 2)) q (j + 1) ∧
      PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal (m + 3)) q (j + 1) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: ONE INDEX OF ONSET BUYS TWO DIAGONALS, NOT ONE. The board's reset step (leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_step_of_black) settles diagonal m+2 at the first black cell of diagonal m+1, one diagonal per index; this says that when the cell it settles TO is itself black, diagonal m+3 settles at the very same index for free. Why it is true: the recurrence reads diagonal m+3 as a one-bit machine whose OR-driver is diagonal m+2, and that driver is black at j+1 in both readings — black at j+1 by hypothesis, and black at j+1+q because m+2 is now periodic with period q from j+1 — so m+3's value at j+1 is the negation of diagonal m+1 at j+2, which already repeats. Hence m+3 returns at j+1 and bool_driven_periodicFrom_of_return carries it forward. This is the lemma crystal 62 asks for by name: it prices the early settlings, the levels that settle before their driver's self-loop is cut, which crystal 62 measures as the entire distance between the truth (slope 1.25) and the reset cascade (slope 2.00). Measured this session (explorer/seeder_ladder.mjs, explorer/seeder_front.mjs): a ladder that uses this rule, the reset rule, and crystal 45's white branch and never consults the truth reaches level 5001 at index 8486 — slope 1.697, and its index never exceeds the wall's budget of 2k at any of 5000 levels — where the reset-only ladder runs at slope 1.989 and is refuted outright at k = 119 (crystal 62: C_119 = 237 > 236). The double rule fires 1398 times against 2201 single steps, and the two-rule ladder's worst ratio, 1.873, falls at level 118, the same event that breaks the reset-only ladder. Separately, on the true front at shift 16, every one of the 1872 early advances in the first 4000 levels is zero-cost — the front crosses two levels in one row or none — so this rule, and not a partial saving, is the shape the early settlings actually have.
proposals.disclaims: Does not prove leftDiagonal_onset_le and does not bear on a prize conjecture — it is a claim about the left edge of the cone, where periodicity is already proved. It is one step rule and not a ladder: the ladder that would use it is deliberately not proposed, because a ladder's hypothesis shape is exactly what killed the previous one (leftDiagonal_onset_le_not_of_black_ladder), and 1.697 is a measured slope over 5000 levels, not a proof that the slope stays below 2. No witness is offered: the hypotheses are periodicity statements, which no finite range expresses, and reading leftDiagonal through evolve costs 3^(j+k), so a naive witness cannot reach index 18 where the first transient lives. The packed-row twin rowNat_return_succ_two carries the witness for the same mechanism instead.

route.tactics:
have h2 : PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal (m + 2)) q (j + 1) :=
    leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_step_of_black m q N j hNj h0 h1 hblack
  refine ⟨h2, ?_⟩
  refine bool_driven_periodicFrom_of_return
      (fun i => leftDiagonal (m + 1) (i + 2)) (fun i => leftDiagonal (m + 2) (i + 1))
      (leftDiagonal (m + 3)) q (j + 1) (j + 1) ?_ ?_ ?_ le_rfl ?_
  · intro i
    exact leftDiagonal_recurrence (m + 1) i
  · intro i hi
    have h := h1 (i + 2) (by omega)
    dsimp only
    rw [show i + q + 2 = i + 2 + q from by omega]
    exact h
  · intro i hi
    have h := h2 (i + 1) (by omega)
    dsimp only
    rw [show i + q + 1 = i + 1 + q from by omega]
    exact h
  · have hb2 : leftDiagonal (m + 2) (j + 1 + q) = true := by
      rw [h2 (j + 1) le_rfl]; exact hblack2
    have e1 := leftDiagonal_recurrence (m + 1) j
    have e2 := leftDiagonal_recurrence (m + 1) (j + q)
    have hd : leftDiagonal (m + 1) (j + q + 2) = leftDiagonal (m + 1) (j + 2) := by
      rw [show j + q + 2 = j + 2 + q from by omega]
      exact h1 (j + 2) (by omega)
    rw [show j + 1 + q = j + q + 1 from by omega, e2, e1, hblack2,
      show j + q + 1 = j + 1 + q from by omega, hb2, hd]
    simp

proposals.statement:
theorem rowNat_return_succ_two (n T p : ℕ)
    (h : rowNat T % 2 ^ (n + 1) = rowNat (T + p) % 2 ^ (n + 1))
    (hb : (rowNat T).testBit n = true)
    (hc : (rowNat T).testBit (n + 1) = true)
    (hd : (rowNat (T + p)).testBit (n + 1) = true) :
    rowNat (T + 1) % 2 ^ (n + 3) = rowNat (T + p + 1) % 2 ^ (n + 3) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE SAME DOUBLE ADVANCE WITH NO AUTOMATON IN IT, in the vocabulary the onset wall's own description tells a seeder to decompose through. The board's rowNat_return_succ_iff advances the agreement front between rows T and T+p by ONE bit per row, when bit n of row T is black. This advances it by TWO bits in the same row. Why it is true: bit n+2 of the successor row is bit n XOR (bit n+1 OR bit n+2), so if bit n+1 is black in both rows the two ORs are both true and bit n+2 of the successor is just the negation of bit n, which the hypothesis says already agrees. Cited by any packed-row onset argument, and this is the reason: leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_of_rowNat_agree needs the low k+1 bits to agree at some row T ≤ 2k, so the front must average better than one level per two rows, and rowNat_return_succ_iff alone gives exactly one level per black bit — a rate measured at 1.989 rows per level, which crystal 62 refutes at k = 119. This is the only rule on the board that moves the front faster than that. Its diagonal twin is leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_step_two_of_black; the two are the same fact in the two coordinate systems, and this one is the one a kernel computation can reach, since rowNat computes row 5000 in a second where evolve gives out near row 18.
proposals.disclaims: Does not prove leftDiagonal_onset_le and does not bear on a prize conjecture. It is a sufficient condition, not a characterisation: the front also advances for reasons this rule does not name, and nothing here says how often the two black bits occur.

route.tactics:
have hstep : ∀ t : ℕ, rowNat (t + 1) = rowStep (rowNat t) := fun _ => rfl
  have hbits : ∀ r i : ℕ, (rowStep r).testBit i
      = xor (decide (2 ≤ i) && r.testBit (i - 2))
          ((decide (1 ≤ i) && r.testBit (i - 1)) || r.testBit i) := by
    intro r i
    have h4 : 4 * r = 2 ^ 2 * r := by norm_num
    have h2 : 2 * r = 2 ^ 1 * r := by norm_num
    unfold rowStep
    rw [h4, h2, Nat.testBit_xor, Nat.testBit_or, Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul,
      Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul]
  have hiff : ∀ a b m : ℕ, a % 2 ^ m = b % 2 ^ m ↔ ∀ i < m, a.testBit i = b.testBit i := by
    intro a b m
    constructor
    · intro hab i hi
      have := congrArg (fun x => x.testBit i) hab
      simpa [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, hi] using this
    · intro hab
      apply Nat.eq_of_testBit_eq
      intro i
      rw [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow]
      by_cases hi : i < m
      · simp [hi, hab i hi]
      · simp [hi]
  have h2 : rowNat (T + 1) % 2 ^ (n + 2) = rowNat (T + p + 1) % 2 ^ (n + 2) :=
    (rowNat_return_succ_iff n T p h).2 (Or.inl hb)
  have hlow := (hiff _ _ _).1 h
  have hlow2 := (hiff _ _ _).1 h2
  rw [hiff]
  intro i hi
  by_cases hi' : i < n + 2
  · exact hlow2 i hi'
  · have hi2 : i = n + 2 := by omega
    subst hi2
    rw [hstep, hstep, hbits, hbits,
      show n + 2 - 2 = n from by omega, show n + 2 - 1 = n + 1 from by omega,
      hlow n (by omega), hc, hd]
    simp

proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_of_rowNat_agree_any (k p T : ℕ)
    (h : rowNat T % 2 ^ (k + 1) = rowNat (T + p) % 2 ^ (k + 1)) :
    PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal k) p T := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE PERIOD WALL'S PACKED-ROW INTERFACE — the thing the onset wall was given on 2026-09-10 and the period wall still lacks. The landed leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_of_rowNat_agree carries the hypothesis T ≤ 2k, because it is aimed at the ONSET wall and must land the onset at k. leftDiagonal_period_le does not care where the repetition starts, only how long its period is, so that hypothesis is pure friction there and this drops it. With this in hand, leftDiagonal_period_le reduces to a statement with no automaton in it: for every k there is some p ≤ k + 1 and some row T with rowNat T ≡ rowNat (T + p) mod 2^(k+1). That is the period wall in the one vocabulary the kernel can compute in — rowNat reaches row 5000 in a second where evolve gives out near row 18 — and unlike the onset ladder's constant it carries no expiry: crystal 57 shows the onset route's constant 16 dies at k = 87867 because it is fixed, while here p is allowed to grow with k and the truth is about 2·log2(k), so the margin widens rather than closing. Cited by any period-wall argument that wants to work on rows instead of diagonals, and it is the companion to the closed leftDiagonal_period_le_of_white_count, which reduces the same wall to a count of eventually-white diagonals — two independent handles on one wall rather than one.
proposals.disclaims: Does not prove leftDiagonal_period_le and does not bear on a prize conjecture. It is a strict weakening of the landed leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_of_rowNat_agree in its conclusion (onset T, not k) in exchange for dropping a hypothesis; it is not stronger, and it says nothing about how small p can be taken.

route.tactics:
intro n hn
  rw [leftDiagonal_eq_rowNat_testBit k (n + p), leftDiagonal_eq_rowNat_testBit k n]
  have hmod : rowNat (n + k) % 2 ^ (k + 1) = rowNat (n + k + p) % 2 ^ (k + 1) :=
    rowNat_agree_forward (k + 1) T p (n + k) (by omega) h
  have hlt : k < k + 1 := Nat.lt_succ_self k
  have e1 : (rowNat (n + k) % 2 ^ (k + 1)).testBit k = (rowNat (n + k)).testBit k := by
    rw [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow]; simp [hlt]
  have e2 : (rowNat (n + k + p) % 2 ^ (k + 1)).testBit k = (rowNat (n + k + p)).testBit k := by
    rw [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow]; simp [hlt]
  have hbit : (rowNat (n + k)).testBit k = (rowNat (n + k + p)).testBit k := by
    rw [← e1, ← e2, hmod]
  rw [show n + p + k = n + k + p from by omega]
  exact hbit.symm

proposals.statement:
theorem stepMod_preperiod_of_return (n N p x : ℕ)
    (h : (stepMod n)^[N + p] x = (stepMod n)^[N] x) :
    ∀ t ≥ N, (stepMod n)^[t + p] x = (stepMod n)^[t] x := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE MISSING ADAPTER BETWEEN THE TWO FORMS THE BOARD ALREADY SPEAKS. Every statement of the onset wall's arithmetic form that a computation or an induction can actually produce is ONE equation: leftDiagonal_onset_le_iff_stepMod_return is one equation per k, stepMod_preperiod_le_of_le_11 is one equation per (k, x), and crystal 61's universal form is one equation per (n, r). The interface that consumes them, leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_stepMod_preperiod, demands a ∀ t ≥ 2k statement instead. This is the two-line bridge: iterating one fixed map from a point that has already returned keeps returning, so one equation at N is the whole tail. Nothing composes those landed theorems today without it, and a prover who reaches the wall with a single return equation in hand currently has to rediscover it before the interface will take it.
proposals.disclaims: Does not prove leftDiagonal_onset_le and does not bear on a prize conjecture. It is pure iteration algebra about an arbitrary function's orbit — it says nothing whatever about rule 30, and it is the only node in this tier that would be equally true of any map at all.

route.tactics:
intro t ht
  obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le ht
  have e1 : (stepMod n)^[N + d + p] x = (stepMod n)^[d] ((stepMod n)^[N + p] x) := by
    rw [← Function.iterate_add_apply]; congr 1; omega
  have e2 : (stepMod n)^[N + d] x = (stepMod n)^[d] ((stepMod n)^[N] x) := by
    rw [← Function.iterate_add_apply]; congr 1; omega
  rw [e1, e2, h]

proposals.statement:
theorem stepMod_preperiod_of_odd (B : ℕ → ℕ) (hmono : ∀ n, B n ≤ B (n + 1))
    (H : ∀ n x : ℕ, x < 2 ^ n → x % 2 = 1 → ∃ p > 0, ∀ t ≥ B n,
      (stepMod n)^[t + p] x = (stepMod n)^[t] x) :
    ∀ n x : ℕ, x < 2 ^ n → ∃ p > 0, ∀ t ≥ B n,
      (stepMod n)^[t + p] x = (stepMod n)^[t] x := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: HALVES THE STATE SPACE OF THE WALL'S UNIVERSAL FORM, USING THE ONE PIECE OF PROVED STRUCTURE THE ROW MAP HAS. leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_stepMod_preperiod asks for a preperiod bound at every width and EVERY start below 2^n; crystal 61 is that statement, exhaustive to n = 31 and the only form of the wall whose induction is not already refuted per level. This says the even starts are free: an even start is 2s, and stepMod_iterate_two_mul (landed) makes its orbit at width n+1 an exact scaled copy of s's orbit at width n, so ordinary induction on the width disposes of it, and 0 is a fixed point. What is left is the odd starts — which are exactly rule 30's truncated left sides with a black left edge, the set crystal 58 identifies as carrying the whole growth of the attractor, and which include the seed, since rowNat_testBit_zero says every real row is odd. Measured this session (explorer/seeder_tails.mjs, exhaustive over all 2^n starts for n ≤ 20): the reduction is lossless — the worst preperiod over all starts equals the worst over odd starts at every width, and the worst over even starts at width n is exactly the worst over all starts at width n−1, which is this theorem's content read as an equation. The same run reproduces crystal 61's numbers independently (worst ratio 1.381 at n = 19) and confirms crystal 57's staircase from a second direction: the longest cycle at width n is 1, 2, 4 stepping at n = 4 and n = 9, the onset-constant staircase.
proposals.disclaims: Does not prove leftDiagonal_onset_le and does not bear on a prize conjecture. It removes half the state space and leaves the hard half: the odd starts are where every measured worst case lives, so this is a reduction, not progress on the bound. B is a hypothesis, not a construction — the theorem is silent on whether any B with the wall's slope exists.

route.tactics:
have hzero : ∀ n m : ℕ, (stepMod n)^[m] 0 = 0 := by
    intro n m
    induction m with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ m ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih]; simp [stepMod, rowStep]
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro x hx
    have : x = 0 := by simpa using hx
    subst this
    exact ⟨1, one_pos, fun t _ => by rw [hzero, hzero]⟩
  | succ m ih =>
    intro x hx
    by_cases hodd : x % 2 = 1
    · exact H (m + 1) x hx hodd
    · have hx2 : x = 2 * (x / 2) := by omega
      have hs : x / 2 < 2 ^ m := by
        have hp : 2 ^ (m + 1) = 2 * 2 ^ m := by ring
        omega
      obtain ⟨p, hp, hall⟩ := ih (x / 2) hs
      refine ⟨p, hp, fun t ht => ?_⟩
      have hBm : B m ≤ B (m + 1) := hmono m
      rw [hx2, stepMod_iterate_two_mul, stepMod_iterate_two_mul, hall t (by omega)]
